signals.state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, as the energy shock pushes inflation up (IBTimes UK). Euro-area inflation reached 4.0% in October, a three-year high, and ECB officials signalled further hikes may be needed (Trading Economics). Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency or inter-meeting move had been made as of 6 Nov.
signals.for_you: Rising policy rates feed through to mortgages, loans and savings rates over the following months. Borrowers on variable rates are most exposed.

signals.name: Undersea cables & GPS
signals.summary: Finnish court convicts Fitburg crew of aggravated sabotage of Baltic cables; GPS jamming spans NATO's eastern flank
signals.state: On 5 Nov the Helsinki District Court convicted the Fitburg's Russian captain and Azerbaijani boatswain of aggravated sabotage, finding the ship dragged its anchor about 130 km and damaged two cables on 31 Dec; the ruling can be appealed (Yle). GPS interference was mapped along almost the whole eastern NATO flank on 3 Nov (Militarnyi). The verdict concerns a past incident and no new cable cut was reported as of 6 Nov, so Watch holds.
signals.for_you: Most internet traffic reroutes around a damaged cable, so users rarely notice. Airlines and ships near the Baltic and Black Sea may face navigation interference.

signals.name: Chip supply
signals.summary: China's rare-earth export pause expires 10 Nov with no formal extension; AI chip shares sold off
signals.state: China's suspension of its rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, and as of 5 Nov Beijing had published no formal notice extending it, though the wider US–China trade truce runs to 10 Jan 2027 (Motley Fool). signals.for_you: Device makers and carmakers that rely on rare-earth magnets are most exposed if controls return. Consumers are unlikely to see shortages immediately.
